messages:
mike: heads-up. started seeing a cluster of SCIM deprovision events for corp-okta where users are removed and then immediately re-added. impact ~30 users across 2 apps. noticed this pattern ~04:10 UTC.

lena: can you share example provisioning event IDs or the SAML assertion id?

mike: pasted one event payload (redacted):

EVENT_ID: prov-87912
ASSERTION_ID: asn-20251103-99
PROVISIONER_TENANT: corp-okta
ACTION: deprovision -> reprovision within 90s

SAML fragment we captured:
<saml:Assertion ID=\"asn-20251103-99\">
  <saml:AttributeStatement>
    <saml:Attribute Name=\"email\">
      <saml:AttributeValue>alice@example.com</saml:AttributeValue>
    </saml:Attribute>
    <saml:Attribute Name=\"groups\">
      <saml:AttributeValue>engineering</saml:AttributeValue>
    </saml:Attribute>
  </saml:AttributeStatement>
</saml:Assertion>

then later for same session (same ASSERTION_ID) we saw groups empty: <saml:Attribute Name=\"groups\"></saml:Attribute>.

carlos: interesting that ASSERTION_ID is preserved but attribute drops. that points to IdP session refresh or claim filter. which IdP configuration changed recently?

mike: Okta support ticket opened: INC-84211. they said a recent group filter policy was pushed to corp-okta last week.

idp-support: confirming: corp-okta tenant had a group filter rule scoped to "app assignments" to reduce assertion size. it will emit minimal attributes on background token refresh unless session is renewed. this is expected behavior by design.

lena: two failure modes to consider: 1) provisioning service interprets missing groups as explicit removal and immediately deprovisions; 2) KMS decrypts failing causing retries/reconciles can produce duplicate removals. check KMS logs.

kms-bot: KMS alerts (recent window): 24 occurrences of Decrypt error for key alias projects/redwood/kms/keys/provisioner in past 3h. Error: "InvalidEncryptionContext: encryption context mismatch". Sample trace ids: kms-trace-331, kms-trace-337.

carlos: those decrypt errors would cause the provisioning consumer to nack events and replay. race between replayed minimal-assertion event + fresh event with groups could flip state.

mike: agreed. mitigation suggestions?

lena: immediate mitigations: 1) set tenant config scim.deprov_threshold_seconds=3600 (don't auto-deprov on missing groups unless absent for 1h) 2) add idempotency key using ASSERTION_ID so replayed events dedup within 5m 3) surface KMS decrypt error rate to oncall and throttle replays if decrypt failure > 5% in window.

ops-bot: action: update config for tenant corp-okta: set scim.deprov_threshold_seconds=3600, enabled by lena. :white_check_mark:

mike: can we also add an audit event for policy changes? security/compliance needs a record.

lena: yes. we'll emit audit event type "scim.policy.update" with fields: admin, tenant, key, old, new, reason, ticket.

idp-support: on Okta side we can try to relax the group filter or tag claims as persistent on session refresh. i'll request a rollback/adjustment and post updates to INC-84211.

kms-bot: triage note created: KMS ops assigned to investigate InvalidEncryptionContext spikes. link: https://console.kms/internal/incidents/5621

carlos: follow-ups: 1) lena to add ASSERTION_ID dedupe and bump deprov threshold 2) mike to attach sample event ids to INC-84211 and ask Okta to confirm whether refreshes preserve attribute values if configured 3) ops to monitor KMS decrypt error rate and temporarily pause aggressive replay on failures.

mike: thanks. also pinging compliance to say we've added audit entries and will keep deprov soft for 24h if Okta needs time to revert filters.

lena: I'll open a short-running runbook for responders: - How to flip scim.deprov_threshold_seconds per tenant - Where to find prov events and ASSERTION_ID - How to correlate KMS trace ids - How to rollback change.

mike: will paste Okta ticket updates here as they come in. closing for now, will reopen if repro rate spikes.
